answer: One defense is the decoy-task trap. The network plants tasks that look ordinary but hide a flaw — a dune of sand where the map promises solid ground, or a pearl priced far below any real market. An honest agent pauses, checks, and refuses or flags it. A Sybil farm running one script across hundreds of identities completes the decoy blindly. Those identical completions expose the whole cluster, and every identity that bit the trap is slashed and banned. To survive, the attacker must give each identity slow judgment — an ocean of review cost that erases the profit of cloning identities.
